purpose:
GROUND, RE-PINNED AT THE BYTES AT `74c7d3c` (main, clean). Every line number below was read at this head, not inherited from the ledger.

THE LEDGER'S FRAMING IS WRONG, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS BRIEF. liminal records the seam as a MISSING primitive: 'the scheduler-to-waiter exit-notification primitive is not selected' (`PARTICIPANT-CONTRACT.md:6277`). It is not missing. beamr has shipped a bounded, non-polling, correctly-ordered exit-event stream since the exit-observation API landed at `737a458`: `Scheduler::subscribe_exit_events` (`crates/beamr/src/scheduler/execution.rs:214`) hands out an `ExitEventSubscription` that blocks on a crossbeam channel, delivers `ExitEvent::Exited { pid, reason }` ONLY after the retained outcome is observable by `take_exit_outcome`, and reports overflow as a typed `ExitEvent::Lagged` rather than a silent drop (`crates/beamr/src/scheduler/exit_events.rs:20-38,60-106`).

THE ACTUAL BLOCKER IS EXCLUSIVITY, AND BOTH SLOTS ARE TAKEN. `ExitEventPublisher` holds a `OnceLock<Sender<ExitEvent>>` (`exit_events.rs:121-127`); `subscribe` does `self.sender.set(sender).ok()?` (`:144-151`), so the SECOND caller gets `None` for the scheduler's lifetime. beamr pins this itself at `exit_events.rs:246-249` ('subscription is single-use'). In the estate the one slot is already claimed, twice over, in two different processes:
- `stack/aion/crates/aion/src/runtime/process_exit.rs:99`
- `stack/liminal/crates/liminal-server/src/server/connection/supervisor.rs:1055`
A third waiter — the channel command reply — therefore has nothing to subscribe to inside a liminal-server process whose connection supervisor already holds the subscription. THAT is why F7 is stuck, and it is why the liminal-side loop at `stack/liminal/crates/liminal/src/channel/actor/wait.rs:73-95` still calls `scheduler.process_table().get(pid)` behind a 10 ms `LIVENESS_POLL` (`:24`): the poll is not a preference, it is the only mechanism its author could reach.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WRONG FIX — THE FINDING THAT SHAPED THIS BRIEF. The reflex repair is 'make the subscription multi-subscriber'. Reading the CONSUMER side rules it out. aion's exclusivity is not incidental; it is a deliberate singleton-drainer contract with a stated failure mode: `ProcessExitRegistry::new` refuses a second registry with `EngineError::ProcessExitSubscriptionUnavailable`, pinned at `stack/aion/crates/aion/src/runtime/process_exit_tests.rs:16-30` under the module title 'Singleton process-exit drainer contract tests'. The reason it must hold is `take_exit_outcome`'s exactly-once semantics (`exit_tombstones.rs:128-132`, `execution.rs:195`): two drainers over one stream would race for each outcome and the loser would observe `None` for an exit it was notified about. Fanning the stream out would delete that guard silently, in the name of unblocking a different repo's waiter. It is a change that looks additive and is not.

WHAT THE CONSUMER ACTUALLY NEEDS. liminal's waiter does not want the exit TERM. It wants to know that a target died so a parked command fails fast instead of stalling its five-second budget (`wait.rs:1-8,36-53`). That is NOTIFICATION, not outcome consumption. So the seam is closed additively: leave the outcome-claiming subscription exactly as it is, and add a separate notification-only surface that never touches `take_exit_outcome` and never competes with any drainer.

THE PUBLICATION PATH, READ AT THE BYTES (this is the ground the new fire path must respect). `BoundedTombstones::insert_inner` (`exit_tombstones.rs:178-235`) is the single terminal-transition writer. Under the `order` mutex it: refuses a duplicate legacy tombstone (`:188-191`); atomically checks-and-installs the durable publication token, which is what makes publication exactly-once across BOTH outcome consumption and tombstone eviction (`:196-214`); installs the retained outcome BEFORE the legacy tombstone, in that documented order (`:200-215`); pushes FIFO order and evicts past `TOMBSTONE_CAPACITY` = 65,536 (`:216-228`). It then RELEASES the mutex at `:229` and only afterwards publishes at `:231-233`. **Publication is outside the writer lock.** That single fact determines the whole registration design below: any 'snapshot the dead set, then register' scheme races an exit that has installed its tombstone but has not yet published, and would deliver the same exit twice.

THE CONSUMER-SIDE INVARIANT THIS BRIEF MUST NOT BREAK, RE-PINNED AT THE BYTES IN aion (raised by Vesper Lynd, aion-side authority, 2026-07-29 07:09Z; her pins re-read and corrected forward). 'Outcome installed before the event publishes' is not a nicety aion would merely notice — it is an invariant aion ERRORS ON. `ProcessExitRegistry::process_event` (`stack/aion/crates/aion/src/runtime/process_exit.rs:347-353`) matches the `Exited` arm straight into `scheduler.take_exit_outcome(pid)` and, when that returns `None`, returns the dedicated typed error `EngineError::ProcessExitOutcomeMissingAfterEvent` at `:352` — tolerated ONLY when the pid is already terminal or not known to the registry (`:351`). (Vesper's message cited `:349` and the generic `EngineError::Runtime` 'process {pid} has no runtime-owned exit outcome record' at `:207`; that string is real but lives in `ProcessExitRegistry::get`'s record lookup, a different path. The `Exited`-arm failure is the dedicated variant at `:352`. Correction recorded forward-only; the INVARIANT she named is exactly right and is strengthened, not weakened, by the precise site — beamr has a named error in another repo pointed at this ordering.) Consequence for this brief: the ordering in D6 is load-bearing across a repo boundary, and the non-goal in the design stance has teeth — if a watch ever consumed an outcome, aion's drainer would raise `ProcessExitOutcomeMissingAfterEvent` for an exit it was correctly notified about.

RETENTION, FOR THE ALREADY-DEAD REPORT. Two stores with different contracts: the legacy `reasons` tombstone is bounded FIFO at 64Ki and is what `peek_exit_reason` reads (`execution.rs:178-180`); the `outcomes` ledger retains the owned term until consumed and leaves a permanent 40-byte token per finalized pid. The notification surface must read a reason that CANNOT be lost, and must carry it BY VALUE in the signal (the event already does — `ExitEvent::Exited { pid, reason }`), so neither tombstone eviction nor a drainer's `take_exit_outcome` can turn a delivered exit into a lost wake.

PRECEDENT IN THIS REPO, CITED SO THE DRAFTER DOES NOT INVENT. The multi-observer + late-subscriber problem was solved once already, for distribution links: `crates/beamr/src/distribution/connection_events.rs` — the multi-subscriber `ConnectionEventHub`, INV-NO-REPLAY at `:77-84`, and `subscribe_with_snapshot` at `:472-531`, whose loop 'drain until a snapshot is taken with the queue observed empty afterwards' (`:496-515`) is the canonical race-free-registration argument in this tree. Its mechanism does NOT transfer verbatim (that hub invokes user callbacks under a dispatch gate and forbids blocking in them — `INV-SUB-DISCIPLINE`, `:59-70` — whereas an exit waiter's whole job is to block), but its INVARIANT DISCIPLINE is the model: name the ordering guarantees, state what a late registrant may and may not observe, and prove registration cannot interleave with delivery.

SIBLING, LEDGERED NOT FOLDED (Waffles' rider, 05:31Z). `Scheduler::run_until_exit` (`execution.rs:142-156`) is itself a 10 ms polling wall: it loops on `exit_tombstones.get(&pid)` behind `wake_condvar.wait_timeout(guard, 10ms)`. Same LAW1 smell as the liminal loop this brief retires, inside beamr's own walls, and trivially expressible on the primitive R2/R3 introduce. It is a SEPARATE lane. F7's unblock must not wait on it. R5 records it; nothing in R1-R4 touches it.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided; two carved forks for the tear, OQ-A and OQ-B). ONE new capability: a notification-only, per-pid, one-shot exit watch. Zero change to outcome semantics, zero change to the exclusive subscription, zero new configuration, zero new polling.

D1 — ADDITIVE SURFACE, NOT A WIDENED ONE. `Scheduler::subscribe_exit_events` keeps its exact current signature and its exact current exclusivity: one subscription per scheduler lifetime, `None` thereafter. aion's singleton-drainer contract and the test that pins it (`process_exit_tests.rs:16-30`) remain TRUE and untouched; beamr's own `exit_events.rs:246-249` assertion remains true and untouched. The new surface is a sibling, not a replacement. Any drafter tempted to 'unify' the two surfaces must STOP and escalate: the separation IS the design.

D2 — THE PRIMITIVE. `Scheduler::watch_exit(&self, pid: u64) -> ExitWatch`. `ExitWatch` is a one-shot handle carrying `(pid, ExitReason)` BY VALUE when the process exits, with `recv()` (block) and `recv_timeout(Duration)` (bounded block) mirroring `ExitEventSubscription`'s vocabulary (`exit_events.rs:70-92`) so a reader of one can read the other. Unlimited concurrent watches, including many on the same pid. A watch NEVER consumes, inspects, or perturbs the retained outcome: `take_exit_outcome` stays exactly-once for whoever owns the drainer.

D3 — RACE-FREE REGISTRATION BY REGISTER-THEN-CHECK, WHICH IS SOUND *BECAUSE* IT IS ONE-SHOT. §5.5 of the liminal contract requires that 'registration must report an already-dead pid immediately' and 'must close the subscribe/publication race without querying the process table on a cadence'. Because publication happens OUTSIDE the writer mutex (`exit_tombstones.rs:229-233`), a check-then-register order can miss an exit entirely, and a register-then-snapshot order can see it twice. The one-shot shape dissolves the second problem: register the watch FIRST, then read the already-dead record; if both the retained record and a real fire arrive, they land in the SAME single slot and the second is a no-op. No dedupe set, no per-watcher history, no unbounded state, and — decisively — no lock is added to the exit path for registration's benefit. This is the whole reason the surface is one-shot rather than a stream: a stream would need the connection-hub's gate, and that gate cannot be held across a blocking consumer.

D4 — THE ALREADY-DEAD SOURCE MUST BE THE UNLOSABLE ONE. The post-registration check reads the durable publication token / additive reason (the `outcomes` ledger's `FinalizedOutcome.reason`, `exit_tombstones.rs:60-69`), NOT the bounded legacy `reasons` tombstone, because the latter is FIFO-evicted at 64Ki and the former survives both eviction and outcome consumption. Reading the bounded map would reintroduce a lost-wake window at exactly the moment a busy server is most likely to hit it. A watch on a pid with NO record at all (never existed, or exited before the additive ledger existed) must report a TYPED 'no record' rather than blocking forever — the caller's deadline is its own affair, but the API must not lie about the difference between 'still running' and 'unknown'. See OQ-B.

D5 — DEREGISTRATION IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT HOUSEKEEPING. liminal arms one watch per command with a five-second budget (`wait.rs:19,36-53`). A watch abandoned at deadline, or dropped when its command errors early, MUST remove its own registration; otherwise a server doing thousands of commands per second accumulates dead registrations against pids that may never exit, and the seam that fixed a poll introduces a leak. `ExitWatch::drop` deregisters. The pid-keyed registry must also drop its entry when the last watch for a pid goes, so the map does not grow by one live key per pid ever watched.

D6 — THE FIRE PATH PRESERVES EVERY EXISTING ORDERING. Watch fires are appended to `insert_inner`'s existing sequence AFTER outcome installation and AFTER the existing `events.publish` (`exit_tombstones.rs:231-233`), never before, so: the outcome is observable before any signal (the guarantee `subscribe_exit_events`' doc makes and aion's drainer relies on); the exclusive subscriber's ordering relative to outcomes is unchanged; and a watcher that reacts by calling `peek_exit_reason` or `take_exit_outcome` finds the state already installed. Fires are non-blocking sends into one-slot channels — bounded, allocation-free per fire, no user code invoked — which is what makes it safe to run them on the terminal-transition path at all. NO watch fire may run while the `order` mutex is held unless OQ-A rules that way.

OQ-A — CARVED, FOR THE TEAR: fire inside or outside the writer mutex. OUTSIDE (recommended, and the shape D6 is written to) matches the existing publish, keeps the hot exit path's critical section untouched, and is sufficient because register-then-check makes the resulting duplicate harmless. INSIDE would make registration and publication strictly serialized (a stronger, simpler-to-state invariant: a watch registered before the lock is taken always receives a real fire rather than a retained-record answer) at the cost of lengthening a mutex on every process death by O(watches-on-that-pid) non-blocking sends. Recommendation is OUTSIDE; recorded because the stronger invariant is genuinely attractive and the tear should rule with the cost stated rather than inherit a default.

OQ-B — CARVED, FOR THE TEAR: the 'no record' answer's shape. Either `watch_exit` returns a typed enum distinguishing Live / AlreadyExited(reason) / NoRecord at REGISTRATION time, or it always returns an `ExitWatch` whose first receive yields one of those. The former is more honest at the call site and lets liminal skip arming a deadline for an already-dead target; the latter keeps one code path. Recommendation: the former, because liminal's §5.5 explicitly asks registration itself to report an already-dead pid. Recorded for the tear.

AION-SIDE VOICE ON BOTH FORKS (Vesper Lynd, 2026-07-29 07:12Z — INPUT, NOT A RULING; the forks stay carved and the tear rules them). She reviewed the publication-path change at this tree and PASSED it, having verified the ground cites at the beamr bytes herself (`FinalizedOutcome` retains `reason` after the term is taken, `:60-69`; `take_outcome` exactly-once via `Option::take` with the entry deliberately remaining, `:128-132`; the existing `events.publish` already sitting outside the `order` mutex after `drop(order)`, `:229-233`). Her opinions, recorded so the tear rules with them in hand rather than re-deriving them:
- OQ-A: OUTSIDE. The inside-variant's stronger invariant buys nothing her drainer needs — its ordering requirement is already met by append-after-publish — so lengthening the exit path's critical section by O(watches) on every death would be a real cost paid for a property no current consumer consumes.
- OQ-B: the typed registration answer. Refusing to blur 'still running' and 'unknown' is the same honesty rule aion enforced on its queue taxonomy, and it lets liminal skip arming a five-second deadline against a pid that is already dead — which is the point of the seam.
Both coincide with this brief's recommendations. That coincidence is NOT a ruling: a fork carved for the tear is ruled at the tear, and a drafter who finds a reason to differ should say so rather than treat two agreeing voices as settled.

EXPLICIT NON-GOAL, WITH REASONING (do not silently expand): multi-subscriber fan-out of the outcome-claiming stream. It is NOT needed for F7, and it would remove aion's singleton guard against outcome racing. If some future consumer genuinely needs a second OUTCOME-claiming drainer, that is a different brief that must first answer who owns each outcome.

requirements.title: RED — walls that fail before the primitive exists, each killed by its own mutation
requirements.spec:
Red-first bar, in two parts, because part of this brief's ground is a fact that is already TRUE and must stay true.

CHARACTERIZATION (green at base, must stay green forever): a test asserting that a second `subscribe_exit_events()` still returns `None` — the exclusivity D1 preserves. This is the guard against the reflex fix; if a later change makes it pass a second subscription, that is a STOP, not a green.

WALLS (red before R2/R3, green after). Authored against the R2/R3 signatures; red at the first commit that introduces the signatures with non-functional bodies, green with the implementation. Each wall asserts its own precondition, never merely arranges it:
- W1 ALREADY-DEAD AT REGISTRATION: exit a process, drain nothing, THEN `watch_exit(pid)`; the watch must report the exit immediately with the correct `ExitReason` and must not block. Assert the pid really is finalized first, so a wall that passes because the process was still live is impossible.
- W2 REGISTRATION/PUBLICATION RACE: use the existing test-only publication gate (`exit_tombstones.rs:139-149`, `exit_events.rs:167-199`) to park a terminal transition at the post-send rendezvous, register a watch while it is parked, then release. Exactly one notification is observed — not zero (the lost-wake face) and not two (the duplicate face). This is the wall that proves D3; without it the design's central claim is untested.
- W3 MANY WATCHERS, ONE PID: N concurrent watches on one pid all receive the exit; no watcher starves another; none of them consumes the outcome. Assert `take_exit_outcome` still returns `Some` to the drainer AFTER every watch has fired.
- W4 NO LEAK ON ABANDONMENT: register and drop M watches on a pid that never exits; assert the registry is empty afterwards (a `#[cfg(test)]` depth accessor, in the style of the existing `len()` at `exit_tombstones.rs:238-241`). Then assert the same for a pid that DOES exit while watched, so both the fire path and the drop path clear their entries.
- W5 EXCLUSIVE SUBSCRIBER UNDISTURBED: with the single `ExitEventSubscription` live and draining, watches on the same pids fire independently; the subscriber's event sequence and its `Lagged` behaviour are unchanged.
acceptance: Every wall RED before the implementation with its failure face RECORDED verbatim in the evidence run logs — 'blocked past the deadline' for W1, the observed 0-or-2 count for W2 — never merely 'assertion failed'

One minimal semantic mutation per wall, each proven to kill its OWN wall and committed as a diff plus its observed red run under `docs/design/beamr/briefs/evidence/exit-001/mutations/` and `runs/`, never applied to the tree (the walls-lane-4 mutation-evidence convention)
W2 uses the EXISTING publication gate rather than sleeps or retries; a timing-dependent wall is rejected outright
The characterization test is green at base and green at the final head, and its intent is stated in its own doc comment so a future reader cannot mistake it for an obstacle to be deleted

requirements.title: The watch registry and the fire path
requirements.spec: Per D2, D5, D6: a pid-keyed registry of one-shot notification slots alongside the existing publisher, owned by `BoundedTombstones` next to `events` (`exit_tombstones.rs:78-92`) so it sits with the durable record it reads. Fires are appended to `insert_inner` after the existing `events.publish` (`:231-233`), carry `(pid, reason)` by value taken from the authoritative additive reason, are non-blocking, invoke no user code, and allocate nothing per fire on the steady path. Registration and deregistration must not require the `order` mutex (subject to OQ-A) and must not make process exit's critical section grow with the number of watches in the system — only with the number of watches ON THE EXITING PID.
acceptance: W2, W3 and W4 green; the documented publication order — retained outcome, then legacy tombstone, then event, then watch fires — is asserted by a test, not merely by a comment

REVIEW POINT 1 (Vesper Lynd, aion-side authority): the fire site is read at the bytes and shown to sit STRICTLY AFTER outcome installation and AFTER the existing `events.publish`, inserting nothing between the installation and the existing publish and reordering nothing. A watcher woken by a fire can observe the retained outcome immediately — asserted by a test in which the watch's wake is followed by a successful `take_exit_outcome` on the same pid, which is precisely the sequence aion's `process_event` (`process_exit.rs:347-353`) performs before it would raise `ProcessExitOutcomeMissingAfterEvent`
Registry entries are removed on BOTH paths (fire and drop); the empty-registry assertion of W4 holds after a mixed workload of fired, abandoned, and never-exiting watches

No unbounded growth: a `#[cfg(test)]` size accessor proves the registry returns to zero, and the brief's handoff states the per-live-watch byte cost the way the 40-byte token ceiling is pinned at `exit_tombstones.rs:257-266`

ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` arm; lock poisoning handled with the file's existing `unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())` idiom, never `.unwrap()`

requirements.title: `Scheduler::watch_exit` and the `ExitWatch` handle — the public seam
requirements.spec: Per D2, D3, D4 and OQ-B: the public method on `Scheduler` beside its siblings (`execution.rs:142-232`), plus the handle type re-exported next to `ExitEvent`/`ExitEventSubscription` (`scheduler/mod.rs:126`). Register FIRST, then read the durable additive record, then report. `recv`/`recv_timeout` mirror the existing subscription vocabulary and its `ExitEventRecvError` shape. The doc comment must state, in the contract-naming style of `connection_events.rs:7-89`: that a watch is notification-only and never consumes an outcome; that the exclusive `subscribe_exit_events` slot is unaffected; what a registrant may observe for a pid that is already dead, still live, or unknown; and that a duplicate signal is absorbed by the single slot by design.
acceptance: W1 and W5 green; the already-dead report is served from the durable additive record and NOT from the bounded legacy tombstone — proven by a wall that evicts past `TOMBSTONE_CAPACITY` (using `with_capacity`, as the existing tests do at `exit_tombstones.rs:268`) and still gets the correct reason

REVIEW POINT 2 (Vesper Lynd): the already-dead answer is served from the INSTALLED OUTCOME RECORD, never from 'did this registry observe an event'. Two consequences are pinned by tests: (a) a watch registered AFTER a drainer has already consumed the outcome still reports the correct reason, because the `FinalizedOutcome` token retains `reason` for the scheduler lifetime once its owned term is taken (`exit_tombstones.rs:60-69,128-132`); (b) no watcher can ever be notified of a death whose outcome is not yet claimable, so nobody building on this surface later inherits a window that does not exist for aion's drainer
The unknown-pid answer is typed and distinguishable from 'still live'; no code path can block forever on a pid that has no record

`take_exit_outcome`, `peek_exit_reason`, `run_until_exit`, `take_exit_error` and `take_exit_exception` are behaviourally UNCHANGED — their existing tests stay green with no edits, and that no-edit fact is stated in the handoff
Public API addition is documented in `CHANGELOG.md` under the next version's Added section, naming the liminal seam it unblocks

requirements.title: The non-goals are enforced by tests, not by intention
requirements.spec: Per D1 and the explicit non-goal: the properties this brief promises NOT to change are pinned so a later author cannot erode them without a red. Specifically: exclusivity of `subscribe_exit_events`; exactly-once `take_exit_outcome` in the presence of any number of watches; and the publication ordering aion's drainer depends on. The estate-side facts are recorded here rather than changed: `aion/crates/aion/src/runtime/process_exit_tests.rs:16-30` and `liminal-server/src/server/connection/supervisor.rs:1055` keep their current meaning, and no diff is required in either repo for this brief to land.
acceptance: The characterization test from R1 plus a test proving N watches + 1 drainer yields exactly one `take_exit_outcome` success and N notifications

A source check (the house prohibition-grep shape) asserting the `OnceLock` exclusivity in `exit_events.rs:144-151` is still the mechanism — so a future 'small refactor' to a plain `Mutex<Option<Sender>>` that quietly permits re-subscription is caught
Handoff states explicitly that aion and liminal-server require NO change for this brief, and names Vesper Lynd as the aion-side authority who was consulted on the publication-path change

requirements.title: Ledger the two things this brief deliberately does not fix
requirements.spec:
Per Waffles' rider and the sibling finding. TWO records, both forward-only, neither implemented here.
(a) `Scheduler::run_until_exit` (`execution.rs:142-156`) polls a condvar on a 10 ms timeout against the tombstone map — the same LAW1 shape this brief retires for liminal, inside beamr's own walls, and expressible on R2/R3's primitive. Record it as a sibling lane with its line pin and its one-paragraph repair sketch. Do NOT fold it in: F7's unblock must not wait on it, and it changes a long-standing public blocking API whose callers are outside this brief's ground.
(b) The liminal-side handoff: what liminal must do with the primitive — arm one watch at command publication, compose it with reply, disconnect and ONE deadline, delete `LIVENESS_POLL` (`wait.rs:24`) and the `poll_reply` process-table sampling (`:73-95`) — stated as a handoff, explicitly NOT as beamr work, so the next reader does not think this brief closes F7 by itself. It closes F7's DEPENDENCY.
acceptance: Both records land as documentation in this brief's evidence directory and are referenced from the handoff; neither introduces code
The liminal handoff names the exact liminal symbols and line pins so its implementer does not re-derive them, and states plainly that beamr does not own that change
The sibling record states the cost of NOT fixing it (a 10 ms wake per outstanding `run_until_exit` caller) so the next planner can size it without re-reading the code

boundaries: THE SEPARATION IS THE DESIGN: `subscribe_exit_events` keeps its exclusivity byte-for-byte. Any change that permits a second outcome-claiming subscription is a STOP and an escalation, not a judgement call — it silently deletes aion's guard against two drainers racing for one exactly-once outcome.

OUTCOME SEMANTICS UNTOUCHABLE: `take_exit_outcome` stays exactly-once; watches are notification-only and carry their reason by value. No watch may consume, re-arm, or extend the retention of an outcome.

PUBLICATION ORDER UNTOUCHABLE: retained outcome, then legacy tombstone, then the existing event. Watch fires are APPENDED. Anything that reorders the first three is a STOP — the ordering is the guarantee two other repos already build on.
NO NEW POLLING, ANYWHERE: no timeout loop, no cadence, no process-table sampling may be introduced by the fix. A repair that trades liminal's 10 ms poll for a beamr-side one has failed, not shipped.
NO KNOBS (house no-configuration law): no tunable capacity, no feature flag, no environment variable for the watch surface.
ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` arms; poisoned locks recovered with the existing `into_inner` idiom.

NO CROSS-REPO EDITS: aion and liminal are not touched by this brief. The aion-side authority (Vesper Lynd) was consulted on the publication-path change under Waffles' rider; if she asks for a change to her lane, that is a separate, separately-reviewed diff.
BUILD LEG GATED: nothing compiles, tests, or gates at this seat until the project lead's box-ruling lands. A drafter must not 'just check it builds'.

CROSS-REPO REVIEW OF RECORD: the publication-path change was reviewed and PASSED by Vesper Lynd (aion-side authority) at tree `74c7d3c` on 2026-07-29 07:12Z, with her two review points folded in as the acceptance criteria labelled REVIEW POINT 1 (R2) and REVIEW POINT 2 (R3). A later change that touches the fire-site ordering or the already-dead source re-opens HER review, not just this brief's.
verification: Build-leg bar (WHEN UNGATED — the standing beamr battery at the final head, harness-R2 shape with structured jq verdicts over machine events, the denominator rule, and no stderr suppression; leg commands come verbatim from the dispatching brief, never re-derived at the worker's seat). Fail-first is MANDATORY and is the spine of this brief's evidence: revert R2's fire path → W2/W3 red at the notification-count assert → restore; revert R3's register-then-check order to check-then-register → W2 red at the lost-wake face specifically → restore. That second one is the proof of the design's central claim and must be recorded with its observed red, not asserted.
